```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
## Every computed table and figure is the paper's own chunk, read from
## report.Rmd, so this summary cannot drift from the paper. Chunk
## options (captions of included figures) are restated in the chunk
## headers below, because read_chunk() carries code only.
rpt <- readLines('report.Rmd', warn = FALSE)
open <- grep('^```\\{r ', rpt)
close <- grep('^```\\s*$', rpt)
ends <- vapply(open, function(i) close[close > i][1], 0L)
labs <- sub('^```\\{r ([A-Za-z0-9_-]+).*$', '\\1', rpt[open])
keep <- labs != 'setup'
knitr::read_chunk(lines = rpt, labels = labs[keep],
                  from = open[keep] + 1L, to = ends[keep] - 1L)
```

# Problem and approach {-}

Validating a predictive biomarker requires an interaction test, which
needs about four times the sample of a main-effect test. Hendrickson et
al. (2020) proposed a data-generating process (DGP) for simulating
aggregated N-of-1 trials. In that original DGP the predictive biomarker
is a correlation with the drug response that is present on drug and
absent off drug. Paper 01 extends the original DGP for the Hybrid
design with carryover. It judges each extension by five criteria:
existence, identifiability under carryover, fidelity to the
pharmacology, analyzability and calibration status. All simulations use
the original response and baseline parameters of Hendrickson et al.
This summary reproduces every table and figure of the paper in the
paper's order. Each is generated by the same code as in the paper.

# Methods

Table \@ref(tab:estimands) states which analysis targets which
quantity. The paired-difference statistic E9 is the one with a closed
form.

Table: (\#tab:estimands) The analyses used in this paper and the quantity each estimates.

| Analysis | Drug indicator | Estimates | Used in |
|----------------------------|------------------|--------------------------------------|--------------|
| Paired-difference statistic E9, E9b (closed form) | binary | on-minus-off contrast, $\beta_{bm:D}$ times the on/off correlation difference | Stages 1, 2, 4, 5; planning |
| The original analysis (mixed model) | binary | the same contrast | Stage 2 (original code) |
| Stress test: the original analysis | binary | the on-minus-off contrast | Stage 6 |
| Stress test: fixed-half-life analyses | $D_{bc,it}$ at an analysis half-life of 0.5 week, the true half-life except in the cells that vary it | on-drug moderation $\beta_{bm:D}$ where the half-lives match | Stage 6 |
| Stress test: analyses with the half-life chosen by AIC | $D_{bc,it}$ at the AIC-chosen half-life (0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 weeks) | on-drug moderation $\beta_{bm:D}$ where the chosen half-life is the true one | Stage 6 |

Table \@ref(tab:ademp) lays out the three simulation studies. They
verify the closed forms, rerun the original code and stress-test ten
analyses under a prognostic biomarker. A fourth run simulates
the analysis G10 for the planning section.

Table: (\#tab:ademp) Design of the three simulation studies in the
ADEMP structure. MCSE: Monte Carlo standard error of a rejection rate,
$\sqrt{p(1-p)/R}$ for $R$ replicates.

| | 1. Closed-form verification | 2. The original code | 3. Stress test under a prognostic biomarker |
|--------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|
| **Aim** | Check the closed-form moments and power of Appendix A, and the loss of power under the original rule | Show on the original code that the correlation rule alone determines the loss of power | Find which analyses keep their nominal size under features the extended DGP adds |
| **Data-generating mechanisms** | The correlation encoding with the original rule and with the decaying correlation; compound symmetry and the separable AR(1) form; carryover on the drug-response mean decaying from the last on-drug value; Hybrid, crossover and OL+BDC designs; $N = 70$; grids of $c_{bm}$ and $t_{1/2}$ | The original `generateData()` at commit 58b32a9, as published and with the decaying correlation only (Appendix B.1); $c_{bm} = 0.25$. (a) Hybrid, $N = 70$, no censoring, $t_{1/2} \in \{0, 0.1, 0.2, 1\}$; (b) four designs, $N \in \{35, 70\}$, $t_{1/2} \in \{0, 0.1, 0.2\}$, the original censoring patterns | The extended DGP (Table \@ref(tab:spec)), run three times: the reported run as defined, the first with the original carryover rule and the second with randomized allocation; base cell separable AR(1), $\rho = 0.7$, $N = 70$, $t_{1/2} = 0.5$ week; 15 null cells (11 without and 4 with a prognostic pathway of strength 0.3) and 26 alternative cells: power curves under the separable form ($c_{bm}$ from $-0.30$ to 0.45, 7 cells) and under compound symmetry ($\rho_{cs} = 0.8$, $c_{bm}$ from $-0.20$ to 0.25, 6 cells), and 13 cells at $c_{bm} = 0.30$ that each vary one feature ($N$, half-life, decay form, dropout, measurement error or a prognostic pathway) |
| **Estimand** | $\beta_{bm:D}$, and the mean of the paired-difference statistic | $\beta_{bm:D}$ | $\beta_{bm:D}$ |
| **Methods** | Paired-difference statistics E9 and E9b, closed form and simulated; the original mixed model fitted with `lmer` | The original analysis pipeline (`lmer`, model-based test) on both versions | Fourteen analyses fitted to the same simulated trials, of which the ten in Table \@ref(tab:prognostic) are reported; two-sided tests at $\alpha = 0.05$ |
| **Performance measures** | Mean, SD and power of the statistic; agreement as (simulated $-$ closed form)/MCSE | Power; mean interaction estimate; number of repaired correlation matrices | Null rejection rate; power; failed fits |
| **Replicates** | 5,000 per cell (MCSE of power at most 0.007); 500 to 1,000 for `lmer` | (a) 500 per cell (MCSE at most 0.022); (b) 250 per cell (at most 0.032) | 1,000 per null cell (MCSE 0.0069 at a rate of 0.05), 500 per alternative cell (at most 0.022) |

# Results

## Stage 1. Validity of the joint distribution

Table \@ref(tab:nonpd) counts correlation matrices that are not
positive definite. The original code repaired 20 matrices (25%) on its
own grid without a warning. The extended DGP stops instead, and it
finds 75% of the grid infeasible at $c_{bm} = 0.6$.

```{r nonpd}
```

## Stage 2. The biomarker-response correlation under carryover

Table \@ref(tab:closedform) gives closed-form power by half-life. Under
the original rule E9 power falls to the test size at every positive
half-life, and E9b keeps a little power from the baseline visit. Under the decaying rule it stays near its no-carryover value
at 0.1 to 0.2 week and declines smoothly after.

```{r cfcount}
```

```{r closedform}
```

Figure \@ref(fig:powerfig) shows the same result as lines, with Monte
Carlo points on them.

```{r powerfig, fig.cap = 'Closed-form power (lines) against carryover half-life, with Monte Carlo estimates (points; 5,000 replicates per cell), under the original rule (constant correlation after first exposure) and the extended rule (correlation decaying at the carryover half-life). Hybrid design, $N = 70$, $c_{bm} = 0.25$, compound symmetry; left panel E9b, right panel E9.', out.width = '85%', fig.align = 'center'}
```

Figure \@ref(fig:gapfig) plots power against the on/off correlation
difference. Power depends on the correlation rule only through this
difference.

```{r gapfig, fig.cap = 'Closed-form power against the on/off correlation difference, with the positions of the two correlation rules. Hybrid design, $N = 70$, $c_{bm} = 0.25$, E9.', out.width = '75%', fig.align = 'center'}
```

```{r m6data}
```

No matrix was repaired in either version.', out.width = '100%', fig.align = 'center'}

## Stage 7. The extended DGP

Table \@ref(tab:spec) collects the choices. The Kind column marks each
element as an extension, a choice, an option or a retained element.

Table: (\#tab:spec) The extended data-generating process. The Default column gives the value of each element in the extended DGP; where the stress test of Stage 6 used another value it is stated. The stress test's reported run uses fixed allocation; its second run assigned participants to paths at random, a driver option outside the extended DGP (Appendix B.5).

| Element | Specification | Default | Kind | Justified in |
|------------|------------------------------|------------|--------|---------|
| Components | $Y_{it} = \mathrm{BL}_i - (TV_{it} + PB_{it} + BR_{it})$, Gompertz means as in the original DGP | original parameters (Methods): BR $m = 10.99$, $r = 0.42$, SD 8; PB and TV $m = 6.51$, $r = 0.35$, SD $10\eta_t$ and 10; $d = 5$; biomarker 124.3 (SD 15.4); baseline 83.1 (SD 18.5) | retained | Methods |
| Validity | stop if the correlation matrix is not positive definite | always | extension | Stage 1 |
| Biomarker-response correlation | $c_{bm}$ on drug; $c_{bm}2^{-t_{sd}/t_{1/2}}$ off drug after exposure; 0 before exposure | $c_{bm}$ below the feasibility bound of every design in the study | extension | Stage 2 |
| Carryover on the mean | decay from the last on-drug value, $\mu_{BR,\text{last}}\,2^{-t_{sd}/t_{1/2}}$ | $t_{1/2} = 0.1$ to 0.2 week (pharmacological, assumed); 0.5 in the stress test | choice | Stage 3 |
| Re-exposure | as in the original DGP: time on drug restarts at zero | on, for titrated drugs | retained | Stage 3 |
| Within-component correlation | AR(1) in weeks, $\rho^{\lvert w_t-w_s\rvert}$, one $\rho$ for all three components | $\rho = 0.7$ (convention; report and vary) | choice | Stage 4 |
| Cross-component correlation | separable, $c_1\rho^{\lvert w_t-w_s\rvert}$ at every lag; the Kronecker form applies to the correlation, since the PB SD scales with the expectancy | $c_1 = 0.2$ (original value) | choice | Stage 5 |
| Path allocation | fixed numbers, as in the original DGP | original values | retained | Methods |
| Prognostic correlations | correlation of the biomarker with TV or PB, or with baseline severity; or a mean shift of TV growing along its curve | off; 0.3 in the stress test; correlations must lie inside the joint bound with $c_{bm}$ (Table \@ref(tab:jointceiling)) | option | Stage 6 |
| Measurement error | independent, SD by phase | off; 3 open label, 6 blinded in the stress test | option (driver only) | Stage 6 |
| Decay form | exponential or Weibull with the same half-life | exponential | option | Stage 6 |
| Dropout | monotone, completely at random or at random given the last score | off; 20% in the stress test | option | Stage 6 |

## Using the extended DGP to plan a trial

```{r planningg10data}
```

Table \@ref(tab:planning) gives the total sample size for 80 percent
power of the paired-difference statistic E9, and the simulated power of
the recommended analysis G10 at $N = 70$. Table \@ref(tab:planningg10)
gives G10 in every cell. G10 rejected the null at `r pg_size_range`.
At the E9 sample size for 80 percent power, G10 power was
`r pg_n80_range` in the `r pg_n80_n` uncapped cells, so the closed-form
E9 rule is conservative for G10 in these cells. Table
\@ref(tab:n80g10) gives the G10 sample size for 80 percent power in
the Hybrid design. It is `r n80_ratio_range` times the E9 value.

```{r planning}
```

```{r planningg10}
```

```{r n80g10}
```

# Appendix A. Closed-form derivations {-}

## A.5 The separable structure {-}

Each step between visits contributes the following term to the
schedule term of the feasibility bound.

| Step | Term |
|---|---|
| on to on | $(1 - \rho_t)/(1 + \rho_t)$ |
| on to off | $\rho_t^2/(1 - \rho_t^2)$ |
| off to on | $1/(1 - \rho_t^2)$ |
| off to off | 0 |

```{r prognosticfirst}
```

# Conclusions

The correlation encoding of the interaction is coherent. The original
DGP holds the biomarker-response correlation constant after first
exposure, so with any carryover the interaction is absent among the
post-baseline visits and power falls nearly to the test size. The
extended DGP lets the correlation decay
after discontinuation, and power returns to its no-carryover value at
pharmacological half-lives. The original effect size of 0.6 relied on
repaired matrices, and a separable AR(1) structure at serial
correlation 0.7 raises the feasibility bound to 0.474. At the
closed-form sample size, G10 power was `r pg_n80_range` in the
uncapped cells. We propose the extended DGP, with a stop on infeasible
matrices, as the reference for simulation studies of these designs.
